modules.title: Data Privacy & Front Office Operations
modules.purpose: To equip Guest Relations Executives with essential knowledge and procedures regarding guest data privacy compliance, identification scanning rules, Malaysian data consent requirements, and front office operational protocols.
assessment_topics: Data Privacy and Front Office Procedures for Guest Relations Executives
modules.completion_criteria: Completion of all checklist items, tasks, scenarios, and achieving a passing grade on the practical assessment rubric.

content.text: Comply with guest data privacy standards by accessing data strictly for business needs, scanning IDs exclusively into the PMS, and permanently deleting scanned copies within 7 days post check-out.
Execute property-specific compliance protocols for Malaysian properties, including obtaining signed Personal Data Consent Notices before recording marketing preferences.
Execute core Guest Relations Executive duties such as reviewing the Guest Incident Log at shift start, contacting VIP/returning guests within 2 hours, and protecting online guest privacy.

content.description: Perform mock check-in registrations ensuring that guest passports/national IDs are scanned solely into the PMS without retaining paper copies, and verify that the guest signs the Personal Data Consent Notice before marketing preferences are recorded at Aurelle Residences Mont Kiara.
content.expected_outcome: Correct handling of identity scanning into PMS, avoidance of paper copies, and proper execution of the Malaysian Personal Data Consent Notice.
content.completion_criteria: Successfully execute 3 test profiles in the PMS simulation confirming no paper copies, PMS-only storage, permanent deletion setup after 7 days, and verified consent signatures.

content.situation: You are working your night shift as a Guest Relations Executive at Aurelle Residences Mont Kiara. A VIP guest arrives at 2:00 AM after a long flight. The guest's passport needs verification, and you receive a message from a colleague on your personal mobile phone asking you to snap a photo of the passport page for a quick room allocation note. Furthermore, you need to ensure VIP contact timing and manage check-in consent protocols.
expected_actions: Refuse to receive, photograph, or store guest identity documents on your personal mobile phone or messaging apps.
Scan the passport directly into the PMS rather than making paper copies or using personal devices.
Contact the VIP and returning guest within 2 hours of arrival.
Have the guest sign the Personal Data Consent Notice at check-in before recording any marketing preferences.

content.question: When must an employee whose role involves guest personal data complete Guest Data Privacy training?
content.explanation: Guest Data Privacy training must be completed within their first week (R-GDP-01-001, GDP-01 §2.1).

content.question: Guest personal data may be accessed whenever an employee feels curious about a guest's stay history, regardless of a documented business need.
content.explanation: Guest personal data may only be accessed to deliver the guest's stay or for a documented business need (R-GDP-01-002, GDP-01 §3.1).

options: It may be scanned into the PMS or kept as a physical paper copy in the guest folio.
It may be scanned only into the PMS; paper copies are prohibited.
It may be photocopied and stored in a locked drawer for 30 days.
It can be scanned into personal mobile messaging apps for manager approval.
content.question: What is the rule regarding scanning a guest's passport or national ID?
content.explanation: A guest's passport or national ID may be scanned only into the PMS; paper copies are prohibited (R-GDP-01-003, GDP-01 §4.1).

options: No later than 7 days after check-out
At the end of the financial year
content.question: When must scanned copies of guest identity documents be permanently deleted from the PMS?
content.explanation: Scanned copies of guest identity documents must be permanently deleted from the PMS no later than 7 days after check-out (R-GDP-01-004, GDP-01 §4.2).

options: Sign the Personal Data Consent Notice
Submit a copy of their utility bill
content.question: At Malaysian properties, what must guests do at check-in before any marketing preferences are recorded?
content.explanation: At Malaysian properties, guests must sign the Personal Data Consent Notice at check-in before any marketing preferences are recorded (R-GDP-01-006, GDP-01 §5.4).

content.question: When must Guest Relations Executives contact every VIP and returning guest?
content.explanation: Guest Relations Executives must contact every VIP and returning guest within 2 hours of arrival (R-ROL-01-003, ROL-01 §2.3).

content.topic: Data Privacy and Front Office Procedures for Guest Relations Executives

rubric.criterion: Data Access and PMS Scanning Compliance
rubric.pass_condition: Zero violations of PMS-only scanning and proper document retention understanding.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates correct handling of identity documents, ensuring scanning is restricted to the PMS with zero paper copies and proper adherence to the 7-day deletion rule.

rubric.pass_condition: Consistently obtains required consent notice signatures prior to marking marketing preferences.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly executes the check-in workflow by having guests sign the Personal Data Consent Notice before recording marketing preferences.

rubric.pass_condition: Successfully demonstrates shift startup procedures and VIP communication protocols.
rubric.expected_performance: Reviews the Guest Incident Log at shift start and adheres to VIP contact timelines within 2 hours of arrival.

modules.title: Fire & Life Safety, Incident Management & IT & Systems
modules.purpose: To equip employees with essential fire and life safety procedures, incident escalation protocols, and secure IT and data handling practices on Day 1.
assessment_topics: Fire Safety, Incident Escalation and IT Security Compliance
modules.completion_criteria: Successfully complete all Day 1 checklist items, pass the practical assessment rubric with a passing score, and finish all assigned quiz questions.

content.text: Execute first-day fire and life safety orientations, locate emergency exits, and apply the RACE procedure.
Identify correct escalation timelines for guest data privacy breaches and staff or guest injuries.
Comply with Property Management System role access rules and personal device connection policies.

content.activity: Complete Fire and Life Safety orientation
Acknowledge RACE procedure and lift prohibition during alarms
Participate in a fire drill every six months
Acknowledge guest data privacy incident reporting protocols
Acknowledge injury reporting timeline to the Manager on Duty
Enroll personal devices in the Mobile Device Management app prior to staff Wi-Fi connection

content.description: Locate and map the two nearest fire exits and the fire assembly point from your primary work station.
content.expected_outcome: A clear understanding of evacuation routes and assembly points specific to your workstation area.
content.completion_criteria: Successfully walk the paths to both nearest fire exits and the assembly point, confirming location awareness.

content.situation: While working at the front desk, you notice a guest has slipped near the lobby and sustained an ankle injury. Simultaneously, you suspect a guest data file was left unsecured on an unauthorized device.
expected_actions: Report the guest injury to the Manager on Duty (MOD) within 15 minutes.
Report the suspected guest data loss or disclosure to the Duty Manager and IT within 1 hour of discovery.

content.question: When must an employee complete their Fire and Life Safety orientation?
content.explanation: Fire and Life Safety orientation must be completed on Day 1.

content.question: Upon hearing the fire alarm, employees are permitted to use the lifts if they are in a hurry to evacuate.
content.explanation: On hearing the fire alarm, employees must follow the RACE procedure and must not use the lifts.

content.question: How often must all employees participate in a fire drill?
content.explanation: All employees must participate in a fire drill every six months.

content.question: Within what timeframe must any suspected loss or disclosure of guest data be reported?
content.explanation: Any suspected loss or disclosure of guest data must be reported to the Duty Manager and IT within 1 hour of discovery.

content.question: An injury to a guest or employee must be reported to the Manager on Duty (MOD) within what timeframe?
content.explanation: Any injury to a guest or employee must be reported to the Manager on Duty (MOD) within 15 minutes.

options: Enrolment in the Mobile Device Management app
Registration of the device MAC address via email
content.question: What is required before personal devices can be connected to the staff Wi-Fi?
content.explanation: Personal devices must not be connected to the staff Wi-Fi without enrolment in the Mobile Device Management app.

content.topic: Fire Safety, Incident Escalation and IT Security Compliance

rubric.pass_condition: Accurately identifies exits and explains all RACE steps.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates full understanding of Day 1 fire orientation, evacuation routes, assembly points, and RACE procedures without lift usage.

rubric.pass_condition: Correctly specifies escalation recipients and correct deadlines in scenarios.
rubric.expected_performance: Applies correct reporting timelines for injuries (15 minutes) and data loss (1 hour).

rubric.pass_condition: Acknowledges restrictions on access levels and staff Wi-Fi connection rules.
rubric.expected_performance: Follows PMS role access rules and MDM enrollment requirements for personal devices.

modules.title: Guest Service Recovery
modules.purpose: Equip Guest Relations Executives with the standards, models, and authorization limits needed to handle guest complaints, accessibility assistance, and sensitive service recovery effectively.
assessment_topics: Guest Complaint Handling and Accessibility Service Recovery
modules.completion_criteria: Complete all checklist items, participate in the role-play assessment covering billing disputes and room-quality complaints, and achieve a passing score on the quiz.

content.text: Apply the CARE model and service recovery authorization limits to manage guest complaints effectively.
Manage guest accessibility needs, evacuation plans, assistance requests, and accessibility-related complaints.
Maintain strict guest data privacy by protecting room numbers and guest names during caller inquiries.

content.activity: Acknowledge assistance requests within 10 minutes and complete or escalate within 60 minutes.
Handle complaints using the CARE model.

content.description: Review the accessibility assistance list for the property and document daily confirmation logs for assigned guests.
content.expected_outcome: Accurate records confirming that guests requiring assistance are contacted daily and their needs are met.
content.completion_criteria: Submit completed daily contact logs for all guests on the assistance list.

content.situation: A guest approaches the front desk claiming their bill has an incorrect charge and expresses frustration. Simultaneously, another guest reports a data privacy concern regarding their personal information.
expected_actions: Apply the CARE model (Calm, Acknowledge, Resolve, Echo back) to handle the billing dispute.
Offer service recovery up to USD 50 for the billing dispute if appropriate, or seek Duty Manager approval for higher amounts.
Immediately escalate the data privacy complaint to the Duty Manager regardless of value.

content.question: What does the acronym CARE stand for in complaint handling?
content.explanation: Complaints must be handled using the CARE model: Calm, Acknowledge, Resolve, Echo back.

content.question: What is the maximum service recovery amount a Guest Relations Executive may offer per stay without Duty Manager approval?
content.explanation: Guest Relations Executives and Front Office Associates may offer service recovery up to USD 50 per stay; higher amounts require Duty Manager approval.

content.question: Complaints involving safety, discrimination or data privacy must be escalated to the Duty Manager immediately, regardless of value.
content.explanation: Complaints involving safety, discrimination or data privacy must be escalated to the Duty Manager immediately, regardless of value.

options: Provide the room number if the caller knows the guest's full name.
Confirm the guest is staying at the hotel before transferring the call.
Do not disclose room numbers or guest names; connect calls to the room without confirming the guest's presence.
Ask the visitor to wait in the lobby while checking the guest log.
content.question: How should callers or visitors asking for a guest's room number or confirmation of presence be handled?
content.explanation: Room numbers and guest names must not be disclosed to callers or visitors; calls are to be connected to the room without confirming the guest's presence.

content.question: Within what timeframe must an accessibility assistance request made during a stay be acknowledged?
content.explanation: Any assistance request made during the stay must be acknowledged within 10 minutes and completed or escalated to the Duty Manager within 60 minutes.

content.question: Within what timeframe must any complaint about accessibility be logged in the Guest Incident Log?
content.explanation: Any complaint about accessibility must be logged in the Guest Incident Log within 24 hours and reported to the Guest Relations Manager.

content.topic: Guest Complaint Handling and Accessibility Service Recovery

rubric.pass_condition: Demonstrates all four components of the CARE model clearly in role-play.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly demonstrates Calm, Acknowledge, Resolve, and Echo back steps during simulated guest complaints.

rubric.pass_condition: Accurately identifies when Duty Manager approval or immediate escalation is required.
rubric.expected_performance: Applies the USD 50 recovery limit correctly and immediately escalates sensitive complaints (safety, discrimination, data privacy).

rubric.pass_condition: Follows privacy protocols without disclosing guest names or room numbers and correctly handles assistance requests.
rubric.expected_performance: Properly adheres to guest data privacy rules for callers and manages accessibility assistance procedures.

modules.title: HR Essentials
modules.purpose: To orient new employees on core HR policies, attendance rules, compliance requirements, and handbook acknowledgements at Aurelle Hotels & Residences.
modules.completion_criteria: Successfully complete all checklists, practical tasks, and pass the knowledge assessment with at least 80%.

content.text: Acknowledge handbook policies, collect staff ID badges, and utilize the biometric attendance clock correctly on Day 1.
Comply with standard working hours, absence reporting timelines, and uniform laundering guidelines.
Meet onboarding e-learning pass mark thresholds and understand coaching review procedures for failed attempts.

content.activity: Read the Employee Handbook and sign the acknowledgement form
Collect staff ID badge from Human Resources on Day 1

content.description: Demonstrate compliance with shift attendance and absence procedures by logging your shift arrival via the biometric clock at the staff entrance and verifying your schedule hours.
content.expected_outcome: Attendance is correctly logged on the biometric clock at the staff entrance at the start and end of the shift.
content.completion_criteria: Biometric record successfully captured and verified against standard 48-hour weekly work schedule.

content.situation: You wake up feeling severely ill and realize you will not be able to attend your scheduled night shift at Aurelle Residences Mont Kiara.
expected_actions: Notify your supervisor at least two hours before the start of your shift regarding your illness absence.

content.question: What is the minimum pass mark required for all mandatory e-learning modules in your onboarding plan?
content.explanation: All mandatory e-learning modules in the onboarding plan must be completed with a pass mark of at least 80% within 30 days of joining.

options: They are immediately terminated from employment.
They must be referred to their manager for a coaching review before a third attempt.
They can take a third attempt without any restriction.
They are assigned to a different department.
content.question: What happens if an employee fails a mandatory assessment twice?
content.explanation: Employees who fail a mandatory assessment twice must be referred to their manager for a coaching review before a third attempt.

content.question: How many hours per week constitute standard working time across six shifts?
content.explanation: Standard working time is 48 hours per week across six shifts; overtime is required to be approved in advance by the department head.

options: At least 30 minutes before the shift starts
At least one hour before the shift starts
At least two hours before the start of the shift
Anytime before the end of the shift
content.question: When must an absence due to illness be reported to your supervisor?
content.explanation: Absence due to illness must be reported to the supervisor at least two hours before the start of the shift.

options: By the end of your first week
content.question: When must you read the Employee Handbook and sign the acknowledgement form?
content.explanation: All employees must read the Employee Handbook and sign the acknowledgement form on their first working day.

options: Uniforms must be washed at home using gentle cycle detergents.
Uniforms must be returned to the Uniform Room for laundering; washing uniforms at home is not permitted.
You may choose to wash your uniform at home or use the Uniform Room.
Uniforms are dry-cleaned exclusively off-property at your own expense.
content.question: What are the rules regarding the cleaning of your work uniform?
content.explanation: Uniforms must be returned to the Uniform Room for laundering; washing uniforms at home is not permitted.

rubric.pass_condition: Accurately identifies Day 1 acknowledgement procedures and biometric clock usage.
rubric.expected_performance: Understands Day 1 handbook sign-off and staff ID badge requirements.

rubric.pass_condition: Correctly states the two-hour advance notification rule for illness and standard working hour constraints.
rubric.expected_performance: Demonstrates knowledge of standard 48-hour work weeks, overtime approval, and illness reporting timelines.

rubric.pass_condition: Identifies the 80% pass mark and Uniform Room requirement without error.
rubric.expected_performance: Recognizes e-learning pass mark requirements, coaching review triggers, and uniform laundering policy.

modules.title: Health & Safety & Company Orientation
modules.purpose: To equip employees with essential health, safety, accessibility awareness, and escalation protocols required during their daily duties at Aurelle Hotels & Residences.
assessment_topics: Health & Safety, Policies, and Orientation Assessment
modules.completion_criteria: Successfully complete all tasks, scenarios, and achieve a passing score on the quiz covering health, safety, accessibility, and company orientation policies.

content.text: Comply with safety equipment requirements when handling chemicals or power tools, and apply proper lifting techniques for heavy loads.
Adhere to night shift break policies and media enquiry redirection procedures.
Complete disability awareness training and engage with the Aurelle culture learning path.

content.activity: Complete the Aurelle Culture e-learning path

content.description: Review heavy load lifting and PPE guidelines in HSP-01 and verify compliance readiness for your shift.
content.expected_outcome: Understanding of the threshold for heavy loads and mandatory PPE for chemicals and power tools.
content.completion_criteria: Acknowledge comprehension of the 20 kg lifting limit and required PPE items.

content.situation: A reporter approaches you in the lobby asking for details regarding an ongoing incident at the property.
expected_actions: Do not speak to the media about any incident.
Refer all enquiries to the Communications team.

content.question: Within what timeframe must employees who meet guests complete Disability Awareness training?
content.explanation: All employees who meet guests must complete Disability Awareness training within Week 1 as per ACC-01 [§5.1].

options: Take a 1-hour unpaid break anytime during the shift
Take a paid 30-minute break between 02:00 and 04:00 and must not leave the property
Take a paid 45-minute break outside the property
Take no structured break unless requested
content.question: What is required for employees working night shifts regarding their break?
content.explanation: Employees working night shifts must take a paid 30-minute break between 02:00 and 04:00 and must not leave the property during it as per HRP-01 [§3.4].

content.question: Which items of protective equipment must be worn when handling cleaning chemicals or using power tools?
content.explanation: Safety footwear, gloves and eye protection must be worn when handling cleaning chemicals or using power tools as per HSP-01 [§3.1].

content.question: What is the weight threshold above which loads must be lifted by two people or moved with a trolley?
content.explanation: Loads heavier than 20 kg must be lifted by two people or moved with a trolley as per HSP-01 [§4.1].

options: Answer the questions honestly with your personal opinion
Refuse to speak about the incident and refer all enquiries to the Communications team
Direct them to the general manager immediately without notifying anyone
Give them a copy of the internal incident log
content.question: A journalist asks you questions about an operational incident at the hotel. How should you handle the situation?
content.explanation: Employees must not speak to the media about any incident and must refer all enquiries to the Communications team as per ESC-01 [§4.1].

content.question: New employees are encouraged to complete the Aurelle Culture e-learning path within their first 30 days.
content.explanation: New employees are encouraged to complete the Aurelle Culture e-learning path within their first 30 days as stated in HBK-01 [§3.2].

rubric.expected_performance: Correctly identifies safety gear rules and heavy load handling thresholds.

modules.title: Information Security

modules.completion_criteria: Successful completion of all e-learning modules, policy acknowledgements in the HR portal, quiz assessment with a passing grade, and fulfillment of all Day 1 and Week 1 security requirements.

content.text: Master core information security hygiene including password standards, MFA requirements, and workstation locking.
Comply with data handling, credential sharing restrictions, phishing reporting, and security incident escalation protocols.

content.activity: Acknowledge the Information Security Policy in the HR portal
Complete Information Security Basics e-learning module

content.description: Verify and set up your secure password and multi-factor authentication configurations for email and Property Management Systems.
content.expected_outcome: Password meets the 12-character minimum length requirement and MFA is successfully activated prior to system access.
content.completion_criteria: System confirmation that password and MFA are active and compliant with security rules.

content.question: Passwords must be at least 12 characters long and must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected.
content.explanation: Passwords must be at least 12 characters long and must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected.

options: Email and the Property Management System (PMS)
content.question: Which systems require multi-factor authentication to be enabled before first use?
content.explanation: Multi-factor authentication must be enabled for email and for the Property Management System (PMS) before first use.

Report them using the Report Phishing button and do not forward to colleagues

By signing a paper document on day one

modules.title: Workplace Conduct
modules.purpose: To establish clear standards of professional behavior, ethical practices, uniform policies, and reporting mechanisms for all employees at Aurelle Hotels & Residences.
modules.completion_criteria: Successfully complete all learning activities, sign the Code of Conduct declaration, complete the required conflict of interest task, and pass the workplace conduct quiz and assessment.

content.text: Understand and comply with Aurelle's core workplace conduct rules, including signing the Code of Conduct declaration, adhering to uniform and grooming standards, and avoiding personal commercial activities on company systems.
Identify and properly report harassment, discrimination, conflicts of interest, and grievances following official company protocols.
Manage unsolicited guest gifts correctly by adhering to established value limits and declaration timelines.

content.activity: Sign the Code of Conduct declaration before your first shift.
Declare any unsolicited guest gifts above USD 25 to the Duty Manager within 24 hours.
Declare any conflicts of interest, including family relationships with suppliers, to Human Resources in writing.

content.description: Prepare a formal written disclosure of a potential conflict of interest involving a family relationship with a hotel supplier to submit to Human Resources.
content.expected_outcome: A complete written conflict of interest disclosure submitted to HR within the required timeframe.
content.completion_criteria: Submission of the written declaration to Human Resources detailing the family relationship with the supplier.

content.situation: A departing guest hands you an expensive custom artwork valued at USD 150 as a token of appreciation for your exceptional service during their stay at Aurelle Residences Mont Kiara.
expected_actions: Recognize that the gift value exceeds the USD 25 unsolicited gift limit.
Report and declare the gift to the Duty Manager within 24 hours.

options: Within the first week of employment
At the end of the probationary period
content.question: When must an employee sign the Code of Conduct declaration?
content.explanation: All employees must sign the Code of Conduct declaration before their first shift as specified in [§1.3].

content.question: Harassment, discrimination or bullying of guests or colleagues is prohibited and must be reported through the Speak Up line or to Human Resources.
content.explanation: Harassment, discrimination or bullying of guests or colleagues is prohibited and must be reported through the Speak Up line or to Human Resources as outlined in [§2.1].

content.question: What is the maximum value for unsolicited gifts from guests that employees may accept without declaring them to the Duty Manager?
content.explanation: Employees may accept unsolicited gifts from guests up to a value of USD 25; any gift above this value must be declared to the Duty Manager within 24 hours [§3.2].

options: The full Aurelle uniform and name badge
Business casual clothing with a lanyard
content.question: What items must employees wear while on duty according to the uniform policy?
content.explanation: Employees must wear the full Aurelle uniform and name badge while on duty, following the grooming standard in Annex A [§4.1].

options: They can be ignored if they do not affect daily work
They must be declared to Human Resources in writing
They must be reported directly to the external supplier
content.question: How should family relationships with suppliers be handled under conflicts of interest rules?
content.explanation: Conflicts of interest, including family relationships with suppliers, must be declared to Human Resources in writing [§6.3].

options: Raise it directly with the CEO immediately
Post it on the company intranet for peer review
Raise it first with the direct supervisor and, if unresolved within five working days, escalate in writing to Human Resources
Escalate it to Human Resources after one working day
content.question: What is the proper procedure for raising a workplace grievance?
content.explanation: Grievances must be raised first with the direct supervisor and, if unresolved within five working days, escalated in writing to Human Resources [§5.1].

modules.title: HR Operations
modules.purpose: To provide intermediate level employees with a comprehensive understanding of HR operations policies, including probation periods, performance check-ins, internal transfers, annual leave entitlements, and sick leave protocols.
modules.completion_criteria: Successfully complete all module tasks, pass the quiz with a satisfactory score, and record the 30-day check-in in the HR portal.

content.text: Understand probation timelines, review intervals, and requirements for internal transfer eligibility.
Navigate leave entitlements, accruals, carry-forward rules, submission notice periods, blackout dates, and medical certificate requirements.

content.activity: Complete the 30-day check-in meeting with reporting manager and record it in the HR portal

content.description: Log into the HR portal, verify your accrued annual leave balance from your date of joining, and submit an annual leave request with correct advance notice.
content.expected_outcome: An annual leave request correctly submitted adhering to the notice period requirements.
content.completion_criteria: Leave request successfully submitted via the HR portal at least 14 days prior to the leave start date.

content.situation: You need to take sick leave for three consecutive days due to illness. You return to work and need to ensure compliance with company policy regarding medical documentation.
expected_actions: Obtain a medical certificate supporting the sick leave of more than two consecutive days.
Submit the medical certificate within 48 hours of returning to work.

content.question: What is the duration of the probation period for new employees?
content.explanation: New employees must complete a six-month probation period, with formal reviews at the end of months one, three and five as outlined in HRP-01 [§2.1].

content.question: Employees may apply for an internal transfer after completing 6 months of service.
content.explanation: Employees may apply for an internal transfer after completing 12 months of service, as stated in HRP-01 [§6.2].

content.question: How many calendar days of annual leave are employees entitled to per year?
content.explanation: Employees are entitled to 30 calendar days of annual leave per year, accrued monthly from the date of joining, as stated in LVP-01 [§2.1].

options: Maximum of 10 days, lapsing on 31 December
Maximum of 5 days, lapsing on 31 March
Maximum of 5 days, lapsing on 30 June
Maximum of 15 days, lapsing on 31 March
content.question: What is the maximum number of unused annual leave days that may be carried forward to the next year, and when do excess days lapse?
content.explanation: A maximum of 5 unused annual leave days may be carried forward to the next year; any excess days lapse on 31 March according to LVP-01 [§2.4].

content.question: Annual leave requests can be approved during property blackout dates if there is a documented emergency.
content.explanation: Annual leave will not be approved during property blackout dates published by the General Manager, except in documented emergencies, as stated in LVP-01 [§3.3].

content.question: Within what timeframe must a medical certificate be submitted for sick leave lasting more than two consecutive days?
content.explanation: Sick leave of more than two consecutive days must be supported by a medical certificate submitted within 48 hours of return, according to LVP-01 [§4.2].

rubric.criterion: Understanding of probation and transfer rules
rubric.pass_condition: Demonstrates full compliance with HRP-01 guidelines.
rubric.expected_performance: Accurately describes probation duration, review points, internal transfer eligibility rules, and check-in obligations.

rubric.criterion: Comprehension of leave policies and notice requirements
rubric.pass_condition: Successfully explains LVP-01 leave application and entitlement rules.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly calculates or describes annual leave accrual, carry-forward limits, blackout dates, and notice periods.

rubric.pass_condition: Identifies the requirement for consecutive sick leave over two days.
rubric.expected_performance: Correctly states the medical certificate threshold and submission deadline.
